children: Subhrojit Mallick New Delhi: The government has brought smartphone screen protectors under mandatory quality guidelines issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards to curb widespread sales of sub-standard products, mostly imported into the country. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology through a gazette notification dated September 21 amended the Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order, 2021 to now include screen protectors for smartphones.

Manufacturers have over six months to comply with the new standards that come into effect on April 1, 2027. The latest move is expected to benefit local manufacturers such as Optiemus Infracom, which has set up a facility in Noida to make screen protectors in partnership with US-based Corning.

Ashok Gupta, executive chairman of Optiemus Infracom, said the company is working to create an additional capacity of 20 million screen protectors at its facility. According to industry experts, the government acted in public interest to curb the flood of low-quality screen protectors imported to India, primarily from China, and to give a boost to local manufacturing. India Cellular and Electronics Association, which counts major handset brands in India as its members, said mandatory BIS certification will protect consumers from sub-standard products.

title: Smartphone Screen Guards Brought Under Quality Norms
